newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr strong on rates prospects,Ldn stocks down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr strong on rates prospects,Ldn stocks down.

text.p: Prospects of higher U.S. interest rates dominated financial markets on Monday, driving up the dollar but pushing London stocks down by over one percent as investors counted the extra cost of doing business.

With most European bourses closed because of a public holiday, most of the day's action was in currency markets where the dollar rose sharply as dealers bet on a rise in interest rates ahead of Tuesday's meeting of U.S. central bank policy-makers.

But the prospect of higher rates had the opposite effect on the London bourse, the only major bourse to open, which shed 53.2 points to 4,640.7 at one point after closing at a record high on Friday. An unsteady opening on Wall Street did nothing to help.

The dollar, after stumbling because of a sharp jump in Japan's trade surplus, gained over a pfennig and clawed back early yen losses in what dealers described as speculative buying, probably from the other side of the Atlantic. Its effect was exaggerated by the holidays in most of Europe which subdued turnover.
Many dealers focused attention on the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Meeting (FOMC) on Tuesday which will set interest rates and thus dictate dollar sentiment in the short-term.
Economists were split over the likelihood of a raise in U.S. rates at the FOMC, but some see the odds improving.

"The markets, up until the end of last week, were of the opinion that U.S rates weren't going to go up.....but the Dow's fall on Friday has made the market stop and think a little bit that its no longer a one-way bet," said Jeremy Stretch, currency strategist at NatWest markets.
"I think it's a close call, one way or the other," said Stretch.

The dollar had earlier taken fright at data which showed Japan's overall trade surplus ballooned 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen ($7.2 billion). But it later climbed to 116.36 yen from its overnight lows of 114. 85 and was at 1.7078 marks versus 1.6944 in late trade on Friday.
A rise in U.S. rates on Tuesday would boost the dollar against the mark and yen after its recent stumble against both currencies as dollar-denominated assets become attractive to investors.
Against the yen the slide has been most dramatic after it was toppled from 55-month highs of 127.46 yen earlier this month to lows of 114.65 on May 15.

In equities too, investors were worried about the FOMC's meeting and London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index fell 1.1 percent as Wall Street made a negative opening with investors worried that higher interest rates would depress profits.
London hit its ninth closing high in the last 11 sessions, at 4,693.9 points, on Friday and some traders said on Monday that a shortage of stock was helping to cap potential losses.
Buit many investors were growing nervous that the record-breaking performance of many European bourses would be vulnerable to any increase in interest rates in the influential U.S. economy.

"Some of the bravado that the market was feeling on the possibility that (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan wouldn't put up rates is evaporating," said one equity salesman. "The market is now preparing itself for a quarter percent increase and anything different from that would really twitch us," he added.
STOCK PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 48.5 points at 4,645.4.
Paris and Frankfurt were closed.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7080 marks and 116.36 yen compared with 1.6944 marks and 115.53 yen in late European trade on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $340.70 versus London's close of $344.75 on Friday. Silver was at $4.71, down one cent.
